records.name: Friends of Bainbridge Green
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Bainbridge Green in Queen Village with the Queen Village Neighbors Association. They weed, plant, sweep, and paint the green, often on City Love Your Park days.
records.what_you_do: Join a cleanup or planting day, often on the City's Love Your Park days. Email the group to be added to the volunteer list.

schedule.text: Cleanup and planting days are held on the City's Love Your Park days, which come in spring and fall. The group publishes no fixed weekly schedule.

cost.text: Free to volunteer. No fees are listed.

first_step.how: Email FOBGVolunteers@gmail.com to join the volunteer list, then come to the Love Your Park cleanup at Bainbridge Green on Sunday, November 15, 2026, at noon.
first_step.basis: Cleanups are public Love Your Park days, and the group says anyone can ask by email to join its volunteer list.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer days are hands-on work on the green: cleaning, planting and painting. The pages do not say how long a day runs or what to bring, so ask by email before you come. Volunteering is free.
first_visit_tips: Email first to confirm the day and start time, since the group's pages list only the Love Your Park dates.
The QVNA events page at qvna.org/events lists each Love Your Park date with its start time.
Bainbridge Green runs along Bainbridge Street between 3rd and 5th Streets, with seating at the corners.

records.notes: Carried over tier 1 fields. Removed the November 15, 2026 date from what_you_do, since one-time dates stay out of that field. The Instagram and Facebook pages were not read. QVNA's page says cleanups are done with South Street Mini Station (see leads_only). The QVNA newsletter sign-up on qvna.org shows an error message, so it may not work.

records.name: Friends of Bardascino Park
records.summary: Neighbors who have looked after Giuseppe Bardascino Park at 10th and Carpenter since 1991. They have helped with renovations and tree and bench replacements, and they organize cleanups.
records.what_you_do: Give time to cleanups, which the group runs from November through April, or donate. Email the group to ask how to help.

schedule.text: Friends-run cleanups happen from November through April. The group has not posted set days or times.

cost.text: Free to volunteer. Donations are welcome, and no membership fee is listed.

first_step.how: Email bardparkfriends@gmail.com and ask when the next cleanup is and how to sign up.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to help with plantings, cleanups or events, occasionally or regularly, and gives an email address to ask how.
first_step.what_to_expect: Helping is free: you can give time now and then or on a regular basis, and donations are welcome. Cleanups run from November through April, but the site gives no set days, times or what to bring.
first_visit_tips: Email first, since the site gives no set cleanup days or times.
The park is carry in, carry out: the site says the trash cans were removed, so take your trash with you.
The group posts updates on its Facebook page, according to the site, so check there for the latest dates.

records.notes: Status changed from tier 1 (active, 2026-10). That date could not be reproduced: the site's newest dated item is a December 2020 history sign, and the site points to Facebook for updates, which was not read. Set to dormant by the dated-evidence rule, so please review before publishing. The /news and /volunteer pages returned 404. The bocce page (bardparkbocce@gmail.com) dropped its connection and was not retried, to stay within the per-group budget. The bocce league may be a separate activity.

records.name: Friends of Beck Park
records.summary: Neighbors in the Queen Village Neighbors Association who clean up and beautify Beck Park. They join the City's Love Your Park cleanups and meet about every two months.
records.what_you_do: Take part in park cleanups and beautification projects, and come to the group's meetings. The group recruits through its Facebook group.

schedule.text: Meets about every two months, and more often during special projects. Days and times are not published.

cost.text: The site does not list a cost.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on qvna.org/volunteer and ask about the next cleanup or meeting.
first_step.basis: The park is public and there is a volunteer form, but the group publishes no meeting days or times and recruits through its Facebook group, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers take part in park cleanups and beautification work, and the group joins the City's Love Your Park cleanups. Meetings come about every two months, and more often during special projects, but the site gives no days, times or location. The site lists no cost, so ask the group what to expect before you come.
first_visit_tips: Email info@qvna.org, the Queen Village Neighbors Association's general address, to ask for the next meeting or cleanup.
QVNA's mailing address is 709 S 5th Street, if you prefer to write.
Watch the events page at qvna.org/events for Love Your Park dates.

records.notes: The clean URL qvna.org/friends-of-beck-park returned 404. The tier 1 URL (qvna.org/https/friends-of-beck-park, malformed) returned the group's text, so it is kept as the website. The newest dated item on that page is a 2020 grant with no month, so status is dormant and last_sign_of_life is left out. The page says the group still meets about every two months, but gives no dated proof. Tier 1's active, 2026-10 did not come from any group page. The Facebook group was not read. Please review before publishing.

records.name: Friends of Benson Park
records.summary: Neighbors who help keep Benson Park clean, safe, and green. They host events such as movie nights, picnics, and cookouts, and they meet every month.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly meeting, help with park upkeep, and join community events such as movie nights and picnics.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the last Thursday of the month, held in the park during warm months and on Zoom in winter. Online meetings listed on the site run 6 to 7 pm.

cost.text: No membership fee is listed. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Come to the next monthly meeting on the last Thursday of the month. Anyone may attend, in the park in warm months or on Zoom in winter.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome at meetings, and it gives an email address for joining the Friends group.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings plan the spring and summer activities, such as movie nights, family picnics and cookouts in the park. In winter the meeting is on Zoom, and you RSVP through a Google Calendar link on the site. The site lists no fee to attend, and donations are accepted.
first_visit_tips: Dogs are not permitted in the park, and children must be with an adult at all times, according to the park rules page.
Sign up for the group's email updates on the site to get each meeting's date and time.
In winter, RSVP for the Zoom meeting through the Google Calendar link on the site.
Email bensonpark1980@gmail.com or call 267-551-1021 to confirm the place before you come.

records.notes: Carried over tier 1 fields. The dated online meeting was removed from schedule.text. The site's hours conflict (6 am to 9 pm listed, and sunrise to sundown stated), so no hours are given. The Aug 18 meeting listing has no year, so it is not used. One-time events are kept out of schedule and cost text. Family picnics and children's parties are listed, which is why families appear in crowd. Event reservation fees are not stated. The group is a project of South Kensington Community Partners (see the top-level notes).

records.name: Friends of Carpenter Green Park
records.summary: An all-volunteer nonprofit that looks after Carpenter Green Park in the Graduate Hospital area. Members help with daily upkeep, park events, and keeping the park safe and clean.
records.what_you_do: Members pay yearly dues and come to quarterly meetings. The group also holds park events and does upkeep work.

schedule.text: Green Team volunteer days run on Wednesday evenings, 6:30 to 7:30 pm, from April through October. Quarterly meetings are open to all and held at the park, moving online if it rains.

cost.text: Annual membership is $20. Higher supporter levels cost more.

first_step.how: Come to a Wednesday Green Team volunteer day, 6:30 to 7:30 pm from April through October, or email carpentergreenpark@gmail.com to get connected.
first_step.basis: The group says anyone can join and that all are welcome at its meetings, and it gives an email address for getting connected.
first_step.what_to_expect: Green Team days are Wednesday evenings from 6:30 to 7:30 pm, April through October, and the page invites people to volunteer in the park. Quarterly meetings are also open to all, held at the park and moving online if it rains. The site lists no fee for volunteer days or meetings; membership is $20 a year if you want to join.
first_visit_tips: Check the upcoming events page for the next quarterly meeting date, since rain moves it online.
Follow the group on Instagram at @carpentergreenpark for the latest updates, as the site suggests.

records.notes: Tier 1 cited the blog for status, but the blog's newest dated post is October 2023 (a pet photo fundraiser). Status uses the upcoming events page, which lists 2026 dates, so 2026-10 comes from there. The FAQ page (carpentergreenpark.com/faq) is linked but was not read, so accessibility and kids policy are unanswered. One-time events on the upcoming page (Movie in the Park, Kids Reading Corner, Love Your Parks) are kept out of schedule and cost text. Instagram and Facebook were not read.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used (Boone Park, no usable result). About 25 WebFetch calls in total, at most 6 per group; no rate limiting seen. Several guessed page URLs returned 404 and are listed in the group notes. Statuses were set from dated evidence only: Benson (active, 2026-08) and Carpenter Green (active, 2026-10) are supported by their own pages; Bardascino and Beck are set dormant because no dated group item after 2020 was found; Boone and Campbell are unknown because the only evidence is the City registry's seen date. Please review Bardascino, Beck, Boone and Campbell before publishing. Boone and Campbell have no group website, so their records carry low confidence. Checked and not recorded: Queen Village Neighbors Association (qvna.org, three pages read) is the neighborhood association that publishes the Friends pages, not a Friends group. South Kensington Community Partners (southkensingtoncommunity.org) is the umbrella named on Benson's site, a neighborhood help desk with no public join program on its page, so dropped with this reason. The Facebook and Instagram pages were not read for facts. The City's Park Friends list page has no entries for any batch group.
